separable: separable — *clog it up*, and *clog up the drain*; it also takes no object: *the filter clogged up*
transitivity: both — transitive (*grease clogs up the pipe*), intransitive (*the drain clogged up*)
gloss: To block something so that nothing can pass through it.
examples: Hair *clogs up* the shower drain every month.
The filter *clogged up* within a week.
Leaves are *clogging up* the gutters.

separable: separable — *close it down*, and *close down the factory*; it also takes no object: *the factory closed down*
transitivity: both — transitive (*the state closed the plant down*), intransitive (*the plant closed down*)
gloss: To stop operating for good, or to force a business to do so.
examples: The diner *closed down* after forty years.
The health department *closed* the kitchen *down*.
Two more branches are *closing down* in March.

separable: separable — *close it up*, and *close up the shop*; it also takes no object: *we close up at nine*
transitivity: both — transitive (*close the store up*), intransitive (*they close up at nine*)
gloss: To shut a business or a building for the night or for the season.
examples: They *close up* at nine on weeknights.
He *closed* the shop *up* early because of the snow.
We're *closing up* the cabin for the winter.

ru: замыкаться, замкнуться; уходить, уйти в себя
separable: no object — intransitive; nothing stands between the two words
gloss: To stop talking about your feelings and become distant.
examples: He *closes up* the moment anyone asks about the divorce.
She *closed up* and stared at the table.
The witness was *closing up* fast.

separable: no object — intransitive; the target follows *on*: *close in on the suspect*
gloss: To move nearer to someone or something, usually in a threatening way.
examples: The fog *closed in* before we reached the pass.
Police are *closing in* on a suspect.
Winter *closes in* early up there.

separable: separable — *close it off*, and *close off the street*
gloss: To block an area so that people cannot get into it.
examples: They *closed off* two lanes for repaving.
The police *closed* the whole block *off*.
Crews are *closing off* the north stairwell tomorrow.

separable: separable — *close it out*, and *close out the account*
gloss: To bring something to an end, especially an account, a sale, or a season.
examples: She *closed out* the account and moved to another bank.
They're *closing out* the summer stock at half price.
He *closed* the year *out* with his best month yet.

separable: no object — intransitive; nothing stands between the two words
gloss: To become covered with clouds, or of a face, to show sudden unhappiness.
examples: It *clouded over* just as we sat down to eat.
His face *clouds over* whenever the subject comes up.
The sky was *clouding over* by mid-morning.

separable: no object — intransitive; nothing stands between the two words
gloss: To behave in a silly, playful way instead of being serious.
examples: Quit *clowning around* and finish your homework.
They *clowned around* in the back of the bus the whole way.
He *clowns around* to keep everyone loose.

ru: вводить, ввести в курс дела; посвящать, посвятить
separable: separable — *clue in the new hires*, and with a pronoun it must split: *clue him in*, never ✗ *clue in him*
gloss: To tell someone information they need and do not have.
examples: Somebody should *clue* him *in*.
She *clued* me *in* about the dress code.
I'm still not *clued in* on how the billing works.

separable: separable — *clutter it up*, and *clutter up the desk*
gloss: To fill a place with too many things, so that it looks messy.
examples: Boxes *clutter up* the hallway.
He *cluttered* the slide *up* with too many charts.
Old apps were *cluttering up* the phone.
